title: Certificación de distribución — CP2, CP4, CP5
scope_note: BLOQUE 5 — quinta certificación contra el árbol de v0.101.22. Cada entrada se volvió a ejecutar sobre este SHA y lo que sigue es lo observado, no lo esperado. El delta respecto a la certificación anterior (2026-10-17, b494bc83 / 0.101.21) es el corte K0 de la línea Kotlin: nueva clasificación de walk KnownUnsupportedGap, kotlin fuera de ALL_TREE_SITTER_LANGS, kt/kts puente a gap tipado en lugar de Unsupported silencioso. Las cuatro superficies (Cargo.toml, SECURITY.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md) re-bumpeadas, binarios release rebuild (cognicode, cognicode-mcp, cogh) a 0.101.22, producer envelope sincronizado. TIER1_PLATFORMS sigue restringido a LinuxX86_64. Per PRF-DIST-05 ninguna plataforma se declara certificada sin build nativo, UAT real y artefacto publicado. CP6 sigue fuera de alcance.
operator_signature: Regenerada por el agente a petición explícita del operador (2026-10-17), durante el corte de v0.101.20. La decisión de certificar y la firma siguen siendo del operador: el agente ejecutó los comandos y transcribió sus exit codes observados; no juzgó ninguno. ANTERIOR: 2026-10-17, head 762acb3a, workspace 0.101.19.

The v0.101.20 cut reinforces this entry: `TIER1_PLATFORMS` in the release-candidate lane now declares only `LinuxX86_64` (PR #361), so the lane's own declaration and the certified catalogue agree — the previous cert recorded the catalogue fix while the lane still declared an aarch64 tier the catalogue called experimental.

entries.result: the attestation script parses its arguments, dispatches to the help path and exits 0 with the documented ADR excerpt. That path exercises the whole argument parser, the `set -uo pipefail` policy, the missing-key guard and the help dispatch.
entries.reason: Re-run at HEAD = d0c12f3d; exit 0 observed. The public chunks a consumer can invoke are all non-destructive from this path (see `scripts/ci/attest-provenance.sh` lines 1-57).

entries.result: a real attestation against a v0.101.20 artefact is not run in this environment. The script requires a long-lived cosign signing key; per the ADR, 'where a long-lived signing key lives and who can use it is a custody decision with consequences that outlive any release'. No key is checked into this clone and no environment variable is set, by design.
entries.reason: Signing-key custody is human-owned (ADR-RELEASE-PROVENANCE-PIPELINEK, 'Open decision'). The script refuses to mint a key and the lane has none to pass. SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE rather than NOT_RUN because the behaviour here is identical on any environment without a key: exit 1 with the documented 'no signing key given (--key)' error. The release operator supplies the key at release time, and that run re-checks the subject digest against the artefact's sha256 (`attest-provenance.sh` lines 224-235).

entries.result: cosign resolves to `/usr/bin/cosign` on this clone. The presence of the binary is what the contract pins; its provenance is not the subject of this entry.
entries.reason: Re-run at HEAD = d0c12f3d; exit 0 observed.

entries.result: no v0.101.20 tag exists. `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 HEAD` returns `v0.101.19`. The command exits 1 with `::error::release-tag-coherence: cannot resolve tag 'v0.101.20' to a commit.` — an unresolvable tag is a failure by design, recorded with its observed exit code rather than hidden. The tag-coherence identity check (tag resolves to the same commit as the build SHA) cannot run until the tag is cut.
entries.reason: v0.101.20 has not been tagged. The lane stage that cuts the tag runs after this tree merges; CP5-02 moves from NOT_RUN to PASS at the tag's own commit SHA. Not FAIL: the missing tag is the gap, not a regression, and the exit code above is the script's documented refusal rather than a broken check.

entries.result: no v0.101.20 SHA256SUMS on disk: `release/` does not exist in this checkout. A three-digest check (candidate digest == attestation subject digest == published digest) needs all three; only the artefact side is missing.
entries.reason: SHA256SUMS is generated by the release-pipeline stage immediately before publishing. None exists for v0.101.20. Recorded as NOT_RUN with the missing artefact named, so a reviewer can confirm the gap is real rather than an oversight. This is the same check that caught the v0.101.11–v0.101.16 asset-set regression from the other direction.

entries.reason: Same root cause as CP5-03: the inventory is produced by a stage that has not run for v0.101.20. The only inventory this repo has ever committed to `release/` in this clone is v0.101.10's, which is what a reviewer can go and check.

out_of_scope: CP6 (web / landing) — excluded by the B6.W5 scope per `docs/roadmap/2026-Q4-CLI-MCP-ROADMAP.md` (BLOQUE B6).
musl / macOS / Windows distribution — `experimental` or `unsupported` in `product/platforms.json`; not certified per PRF-DIST-05.

Linux aarch64 certification — `experimental` in the catalogue with evidence of verified absence, and since PR #361 `TIER1_PLATFORMS` no longer declares it, so the release lane does not claim to build it. The cross-build lane exists but no native aarch64 runner was exercised, so no cross-built artefact is promoted to certified. TF-7 tracks provisioning the lane.
notes: Every NOT_RUN / SKIP_NOT_APPLICABLE entry carries a `reason`. The companion suite `crates/cognicode-core/tests/b6_w5_distribution_certification.rs` enforces that with `no_silent_skips` and `no_unjustified_not_run`, so a later commit cannot quietly drop a justification.

No `FAIL` is recorded. A FAIL would mean a script that exists and is supposed to run on this clone returned non-zero and the check itself was the thing that broke. The one non-zero exit recorded here (CP5-02, exit 1) is the script's documented refusal for a tag that does not exist yet, which is why its status is NOT_RUN and not FAIL.

`head_sha` and `cp5_workspace_version` are checkable: `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` reads both and asserts the version equals `Cargo.toml`. This cert is the thing that test exists to keep honest, which is why a stale one fails the gate instead of quietly passing.

What changed against the 2026-10-17 cert for v0.101.19: the workspace version moved 0.101.19 → 0.101.20 and every version reference in the commands and texts moved with it; CP2-01, CP2-03, CP2-04, CP4-01, CP4-03 and CP5-01 were re-executed at SHA d0c12f3d and the observed exit codes are recorded; CP2-02, CP4-02, CP5-02, CP5-03 and CP5-04 remain in their honest non-PASS states for the same missing-artefact / missing-key / missing-tag reasons, now stated against v0.101.20 and against `release/` being absent from this checkout rather than holding stale artefacts.

The v0.101.19 cert's CP2-02 result text described the `release/` directory of the shared checkout, which held v0.101.10 artefacts. This regeneration states plainly that `release/` does not exist in the checkout the commands ran in, instead of describing a directory that a reviewer would not find.

Regeneration of 2026-10-17 (corte v0.101.20): the cert was updated to record HEAD = d0c12f3d and workspace v0.101.20. The B6.W5 cert moves with every workspace version bump by design (the contract `cp5_workspace_version_consistent` enforces that the cert cannot disagree with `Cargo.toml`); v0.101.20 is the CU-1 reliable-consumption-SDK cut whose release lane can actually satisfy `TIER1_PLATFORMS` (PR #361).
